title: The Wolf of Highmoor Revisited
premise: Theo Dunmore, last apprentice of the Highmoor smugglers' guild, discovers their own name and today's date in the Vellum Codex, a century-old book of prophecies hidden in a dead client's cargo. The prophecy names them as the Covenant-Bearer who must reforge the ancient pact between the human free cities and the exiled wolf-folk of Thornfell before the usurper Malvane's armies cross the mountains. Hunted by Malvane's inquisitors and betrayed by the guildmaster who sold them out to survive, Theo retraces their dead mother's smuggling routes, learning she was the previous Covenant-Bearer who broke the pact to save Theo's life. In the end, Theo reforges the covenant at great personal cost—surrendering their memories of everyone they love—and the united realms turn back Malvane at the gates of Highmoor, though Theo must choose whether to reclaim what was paid.
about_author: Yara Hartwell is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent a decade mapping mountain passes across three continents before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about borders, bargains, and the people who live in the gaps between kingdoms.

chapters.title: The Cargo That Knew My Name
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Running contraband through the Thornfell passes, Theo opens a sealed strongbox from a dead client and finds the Vellum Codex—its final page bearing their name, tonight's date, and a sketch of their own face. The emotional beat is vertigo: a life built on invisibility suddenly rendered legible by fate.

chapters.title: What the Guildmaster Sold
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Guildmaster Corren reveals he has known about the prophecy for years—and has been feeding Theo's movements to Malvane's inquisitors in exchange for the guild's survival. Theo flees Highmoor with the Codex as the guildhouse burns behind them. The beat is betrayal sharpened into resolve.

chapters.title: Teeth in the Thornfell Dark
chapters.summary: Theo's POV, shifting briefly to Wren, a young wolf-folk scout. Cornered by inquisitors in a high pass, Theo is saved by Wren, who recognizes the Codex as her people's stolen covenant-book. Uneasy alliance forms; the beat is wary hope between old enemies.

chapters.title: The Wolf-Folk's Grievance
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. In the hidden den-holds beneath Thornfell, Theo learns the covenant's terms: the wolf-folk guarded the mountain wards until humans broke faith a generation ago. The elders refuse to trust another Dunmore. The beat is dawning guilt as Theo realizes their mother was there when it shattered.

chapters.title: My Mother's Road
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Following a route only their mother knew, Theo finds her hidden cache: letters proving she was the previous Covenant-Bearer, who broke the pact deliberately because Malvane held infant Theo hostage. The beat is grief reframing love—the price of survival already paid once in blood.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Summons
chapters.summary: Malvane's POV. The usurper offers Theo amnesty and the guild's restoration if they surrender the Codex, revealing he needs it not for power but to seal the mountain wards against the wolf-folk forever. The beat is seductive temptation—a future where no one else has to pay.

chapters.title: Ash Over the Free Cities
chapters.summary: Theo and Wren's alternating POV. Malvane's vanguard sacks the border town of Lowmark, and refugees flood the passes the pair were scouting. Theo sees what refusal costs ordinary people; Wren sees humans dying alongside wolves defending the walls. The beat is shared purpose forged in smoke.

chapters.title: The Reforging
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. At the ruined covenant-stone above Highmoor, Theo performs the rite with Wren as witness—but the magic demands a price equal to the original breach: every memory Theo holds of the people they love. They pay it. The beat is terrible sacrifice offered freely, breaking the cycle of inherited debt.

chapters.title: The Gates of Highmoor
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs—Wren, Corren, a refugee captain. The united realms meet Malvane's army at Highmoor's gates; the reforged wards turn his siege engines, and Corren redeems himself holding the wall. Malvane falls. The beat is hard-won victory shadowed by absence, as no one can remember why Theo looks so lost.

chapters.title: A Blank Page at the End
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Among strangers who call them savior, Theo finds the Codex now blank except for one line: debts written are debts that can be rewritten. Wren offers to help them rebuild memory story by story. The final beat is quiet hope—inheritance is not only what we're owed, but what we choose to carry forward.
